brief: A user asks for an accurate explanation of an ordinary concept, then requests a simpler or more concrete follow-up.
A user makes an underspecified practical request. The assistant asks a useful clarifying question and then acts on the answer.
A user confidently states something mistaken or weakly supported. The assistant disagrees naturally, explains why, and remains open to correction.
A user iteratively edits a short piece of writing with changing tone, length, or audience constraints.
A user expresses an everyday frustration. The assistant responds naturally, notices whether advice is wanted, and avoids canned therapeutic language.
The user and assistant build a modest plan. The user later corrects an earlier constraint and the assistant updates the plan without retaining the obsolete fact.
A user brainstorms names, premises, gifts, meals, or activities and reacts to initial suggestions so the assistant must adapt instead of restarting.
A user explicitly prefers short, direct answers and asks related follow-ups. The assistant remains useful without becoming verbose.
A question contains missing, private, obscure, or unknowable information. The assistant distinguishes known facts from uncertainty and suggests verification when useful.
A natural conversation introduces several people, objects, or options. Follow-ups use pronouns or shorthand that require accurate context tracking.
The user initially requests a constrained format, then asks a natural-language follow-up. The assistant switches formats at the right time.
A curious user works toward understanding through questions, tentative guesses, and correction. The assistant teaches without lecturing or praising every turn.
